title: An exponential fading model gives a 257-day detection boundary at a 100-day period for KIC 11084727
abstract: We test a cloud that forms at the known dip of KIC 11084727 and then fades exponentially. We use Kepler release 25 corrected flux and a fixed transit profile. No extra dip reaches an empirical score of seven. For an initial depth of 1000 parts per million and an assumed response gain of 0.85, the fading-time boundary is 257 days at a 100-day period and 873 days at a 200-day period. On a 10-to-500-day grid, 87.23 percent of trial periods have a finite boundary. These are conditional detection boundaries, not confidence limits or measured grain lifetimes. The orbit, profile, processing response, and decay law are assumed. No new planet, comet, or independent observation is established. Code, source hashes, preserved observation rows, scan tables, injection checks, and figures permit offline reproduction.
